cues.en: In the early days of Twitter, it was like a place of radical deshaming.
cues.zh: 在 Twitter 早期，那里就像是一个彻底消除羞耻感的地方。

cues.en: People would admit shameful secrets about themselves,
cues.zh: 人们会坦白自己难以启齿的秘密，

cues.en: and other people would say, oh my god, I'm exactly the same.
cues.zh: 而其他人会说：“我的天，我也完全一样。”

cues.en: Voiceless people realized that they had a voice, and it was powerful and eloquent.
cues.zh: 没有发声渠道的人意识到自己拥有了话语权，而且强大又有力。

cues.en: If a newspaper
cues.zh: 如果有报纸

cues.en: ran some racist or homophobic
cues.zh: 刊登了带有种族歧视或恐同倾向的

cues.en: column, we realized we could do something about it. We could get them. We could hit them with a weapon that we understood, but they didn't, The social media shaming.
cues.zh: 专栏文章，我们意识到我们可以采取行动了。我们可以收拾他们，用一种我们熟悉而他们陌生的武器去打击他们——那就是社交媒体上的公开羞辱。

cues.en: Advertisers would withdraw their advertising.
cues.zh: 广告商会撤回赞助。

cues.en: When powerful people misused their privilege,
cues.zh: 当权贵滥用特权时，

cues.en: we were going to get them.
cues.zh: 我们就能让他们付出代价。

cues.en: This was like the democratization
cues.zh: 这就像是正义的

cues.en: of justice.
cues.zh: 民主化普及。

cues.en: Hierarchies were being leveled out.
cues.zh: 阶层壁垒正在被抹平。

cues.en: We were going to do things better.
cues.zh: 我们本可以让事情变得更好。

cues.en: Soon after that, a disgraced pop science writer called Jonah Larra, he'd been caught plagiarizing
cues.zh: 不久之后，一位名誉扫地的科普作家 Jonah Larra，他被抓到抄袭

cues.en: and faking quotes,
cues.zh: 并伪造引言，

cues.en: and he was drenched in shame and regret, he told me. And he had the opportunity
cues.zh: 他告诉我，当时他整个人被羞愧与悔恨彻底吞噬。随后他获得了一个机会，

cues.en: to publicly apologize at a foundation lunch.
cues.zh: 在一家基金会的午餐会上公开道歉。

cues.en: This is going to be the most important speech of his life. Maybe it would win him some salvation.
cues.zh: 这将是他人生中最重要的一场演讲，或许能为他换来一丝救赎。

cues.en: He knew before he arrived that the foundation was going to be live streaming his event, but what he didn't know until he turned up was that they directed a giant screen Twitter feed right next to his head.
cues.zh: 他在到场前就知道基金会会直播这次活动，但他到了现场才发现，他们竟然在他头部正旁边立了一块巨幕，实时滚动播放 Twitter 评论。

cues.en: Another word in a monitor screen in his eye line. You know, I don't think the foundation did this because they were monstrous.
cues.zh: 视线范围内还有一块监视屏。其实我觉得基金会这么做并不是因为他们有多残忍。

cues.en: I think they were clueless. I think this was a unique moment when the beautiful naivety of Twitter was hitting the increasingly horrific reality.
cues.zh: 我觉得他们当时一头雾水。我觉得这是一个独特的时刻，Twitter 那种天真的美好，撞上了愈发可怕的现实。

cues.en: Here were some of the tweets that were cascading into his eyeline as he was trying to apologize.
cues.zh: 这些推文不断涌入他的视线，而他正试图道歉。

cues.en: Joan Olera
cues.zh: Joan Olera

cues.en: boring us into forgiving him.
cues.zh: 无聊到让我们原谅他。

cues.en: And Joan Olera has not proven that he is capable of feeling shame.
cues.zh: 而 Joan Olera 并没有证明他有羞耻心。

cues.en: That one must have been written by the best psychiatrist
cues.zh: 那条一定是出自最顶尖的精神科医生之手

cues.en: ever
cues.zh: 有史以来

cues.en: to know that about such a tiny figure behind the lectern.
cues.zh: 才能看透讲台后面那么小个子的一个人。

cues.en: And Joe Valera is just a frigging sociopath.
cues.zh: 而 Joe Valera 就是个彻头彻尾的反社会。

cues.en: That last word, it's a very human thing to do, to dehumanize the people we hurt. It's because we want to destroy people but not feel bad about it.
cues.zh: 最后那个词，去人性化我们伤害的人，这其实是很人性的事。因为我们想毁掉别人，却又不想为此感到内疚。

cues.en: Imagine if this was an actual court,
cues.zh: 想象一下，如果这是一个真实的法庭，

cues.en: and the accused was in the dock begging for another chance, and the jury was yelling out, Bored,

cues.en: Sociopath.

cues.en: You know, when we watch courtroom dramas, we tend to identify with the kind hearted defense attorney
cues.zh: 你知道，我们看庭审剧时，往往会认同那位心地善良的辩护律师

cues.en: that give us the power, and we become like hanging judges.
cues.zh: 那给了我们力量，我们变成了冷酷的判官。

cues.en: Power shifts fast.
cues.zh: 权力转移得很快。

cues.en: We were getting Jonah because he was perceived to have misused his privilege,
cues.zh: 我们当初针对 Jonah，是因为大家觉得他滥用了自己的特权，

cues.en: but Jonah was on the floor then, and we were still kicking and congratulating

cues.en: ourselves for punching up.
cues.zh: 敢于挑战强者而沾沾自喜。

cues.en: And it began to feel weird and empty when there wasn't a powerful person who had misused their privilege that we could get.
cues.zh: 当没有一个滥用特权的强者可供我们攻击时，就开始觉得怪异而空虚。

cues.en: A day without a shaming began to feel like a day picking fingernails
cues.zh: 没有羞辱对象的一天，开始像是抠指甲

cues.en: and treading water.
cues.zh: 和原地踏步的一天。

cues.zh: 让我给你讲个故事。

cues.en: It's about a woman called Justine Sacco.
cues.zh: 故事的主人公是一位名叫 Justine Sacco 的女性。

cues.zh: 她是一名来自纽约的公关人员，Twitter 上只有 170 个

cues.en: So Justine chuckled to herself and pressed send

cues.en: and got no replies
cues.zh: 但没有人回复。

cues.en: And she had a little time to spare before her final leg, so she thought up another funny little acerbic joke.
cues.zh: 距离下一段航程起飞还有一点时间，于是她又想出了一个有趣又犀利的小笑话。

cues.en: And

cues.zh: 她暗自笑了笑，

cues.zh: 事情的经过是这样的：她的 170 个粉丝中，有一个人把那条推文转发给了 Gawker 的一名记者，而这名记者又把它转发给了自己的 1.5 万名

cues.en: followers.
cues.zh: 粉丝。

cues.zh: 几周后，我联系了 Gawker 的那位记者。我给他发了封邮件，问他当时是什么感觉。他说，那种感觉简直妙不可言。

cues.zh: 然后他说，

cues.zh: 但她并不好，

cues.zh: 因为就在她睡觉时，Twitter 控制了她的生活，并把它一点一点拆碎。

cues.zh: 笑话也像刷了我的屏那样，刷爆了你的 Twitter 信息流吗？确实刷爆了我的，那晚我和所有人想的一样，那就是，哇，

cues.zh: 有人的生活即将变得很糟。我从床上坐起来，把枕头垫在脑后，然后

cues.zh: 我想，

cues.en: I'm not entirely sure that joke was intended to be racist.
cues.zh: 我不太确定那个笑话是故意带种族主义色彩的。

cues.en: Maybe instead of gleefully flaunting her privilege, she was mocking the gleeful flaunting of privilege. There is a comedy tradition of this, like South Park or Colbert or Randy Newman.
cues.zh: 也许她不是在兴高采烈地炫耀自己的特权，而是在嘲讽那种兴高采烈地炫耀特权。喜剧里有个传统，比如 South Park、Colbert 或 Randy Newman。

cues.zh: 生活在美国，会让我们对第三世界正在发生的事处在某种泡泡里。我是在拿那个泡泡开玩笑。

cues.en: You know, another woman on Twitter that night, a New Statesman writer, Helen Lewis, she reviewed my book on public shaming and wrote that she tweeted that night, I'm not sure that
cues.zh: 你知道，那天晚上 Twitter 上还有另一个女人，New Statesman 的撰稿人 Helen Lewis，她评论了我那本关于公开羞辱的书，还写道她那晚发推说，我不确定

cues.zh: 接着就有人呼吁解雇她。

cues.zh: 全世界成千上万的人认定，他们有责任让她被解雇。

cues.zh: 那晚很多公司赚得盆满钵满。要知道，Justine 的名字平时一个月才被谷歌搜索 40 次。

到 46.8 万美元

cues.zh: 你能想到比这更不公正的事吗？Justine在飞机上睡着了，无法为自己辩解，而她的无能为力

cues.zh: 如果你想知道因为某个被误解的……而发现自己刚刚被批得体无完肤是什么感觉

cues.zh: 在那之前，她工作

cues.en: with adults with learning difficulties and was apparently really good at her job.
cues.zh: 照顾有学习障碍的成年人，而且显然非常擅长她的工作。

cues.en: Justine was fired, of course, because social media demanded it.
cues.zh: Justine当然被解雇了，因为社交媒体要求如此。

cues.en: But it was worse than that. She was losing herself.
cues.zh: 但情况比这更糟。她在失去自我。

cues.en: She was waking up in the middle of the night, forgetting who she was.
cues.zh: 她半夜醒来，忘记自己是谁。

cues.en: She was got because she was perceived to have misused her privilege. And of course, that's a much better thing to get people for than the things we used to get people for, like having children out of wedlock.
cues.zh: 她遭到围攻，是因为人们认为她滥用了自己的特权。当然，比起过去人们被围攻的理由——比如未婚生子——这确实是个更好的理由。

cues.en: But the phrase misuse of privilege is becoming a free pass to tear apart pretty much anybody we choose to.
cues.zh: 但“滥用特权”这个说法，正变成一张免费通行证，让我们几乎可以撕裂任何我们想撕裂的人。

cues.en: It's becoming a devalued
cues.zh: 它正在变成一个贬值的

cues.en: term,
cues.zh: 词，

cues.en: and it's making us lose our capacity for empathy and for distinguishing
cues.zh: 它正在让我们丧失同理心和分辨

cues.en: between serious and unserious
cues.zh: 严重与不严重

cues.en: transgressions.
cues.zh: 越界行为的能力。

cues.en: Justine had 170 Twitter followers, and so to make it work, she had to be fictionalized.
cues.zh: Justine只有170个推特粉丝，所以为了让这事成立，她必须被虚构化。

cues.en: Word got around that she was the daughter of the mining billionaire,
cues.zh: 有传言说她是矿业亿万富翁的女儿，

cues.en: Desmond Sacco.
cues.zh: Desmond Sacco。

cues.en: I thought that was true about Justine until I met her at a bar and I asked her about her billionaire father, and she said, my father sells carpets.
cues.zh: 我原以为Justine也是这样，直到我在酒吧遇到她，问起她那亿万富翁父亲的事，她说，我父亲是卖地毯的。

cues.en: And I think back on the early days of Twitter, when people would admit shameful secrets about themselves, and other people would say, oh my god, I'm exactly the same.
cues.zh: 我回想起Twitter的早期，那时人们会承认自己不光彩的秘密，其他人会说，天哪，我完全一样。

cues.en: These days, the hunt is on for people's shameful secrets.
cues.zh: 如今，人们却在到处搜寻别人不光彩的秘密。

cues.en: You can lead a good ethical life, but some bad phraseology in a tweet can overwhelm it all, become a clue to your secret inner evil.
cues.zh: 你可以过一种有道德的好生活，但推文里的一些糟糕措辞就能压倒这一切，成为你内心隐秘邪恶的线索。

cues.en: Maybe there's two types of people in the world, those people who favor humans over ideology
cues.zh: 也许世界上有两种人，一种人看重人胜过意识形态，

cues.en: and those people who favor ideology over humans.
cues.zh: 另一种人看重意识形态胜过人。

cues.en: I favor humans over ideology,
cues.zh: 我看重人胜过意识形态，

cues.en: but right now, the ideologues are winning, and they're creating a stage for constant
cues.zh: 但现在，意识形态至上者正在获胜，他们在搭建一个舞台，不断上演

cues.en: artificial high dramas,
cues.zh: 人为的激烈戏剧，

cues.en: where everybody's either a magnificent hero or a sickening villain, even though we know that's not true about our fellow humans. What's true is that we are clever and stupid.
cues.zh: 每个人要么是伟大的英雄，要么是令人作呕的恶棍，尽管我们知道我们的同类并非如此。真实的是，我们既聪明又愚蠢。

cues.en: What's true is that we're gray areas.
cues.zh: 真实的是，我们都身处灰色地带。

cues.en: The great thing about social media was how it gave a voice to voiceless people, but we're now creating a surveillance society where the smartest way to survive is to go back to being voiceless.
cues.zh: 社交媒体的伟大之处在于它让无声者有了声音，但我们现在正在创造一个监控社会，其中最聪明的生存方式就是重新变得无声。

cues.en: Let's not do that. Thank you.
cues.zh: 我们别那样做。谢谢。

cues.en: Thank you, John. Thanks, Gilda.
cues.zh: 谢谢你，John。谢谢，Gilda。

cues.en: Don't go away.
cues.zh: 别走开。

cues.en: What
cues.zh: 什么？

cues.en: what strikes me about Justine's story is also the fact that if you Google her name today, this story covers the first 100 pages of Google results. There is nothing else about her.
cues.zh: 令我印象深刻的是，贾斯汀的故事还有一点：如果你今天在 Google 上搜索她的名字，这个故事会占据 Google 搜索结果的前 100 页。关于她，再也找不到别的内容了。

cues.en: In your book, you mention another story of another victim who actually got taken on by a reputation management firm and by,
cues.zh: 你在书中还提到过另一个受害者的故事。她后来被一家声誉管理公司接手，并通过……

cues.en: you know, creating blogs and posting nice, innocuous stories about her love for cats and holidays and these kind of things. They managed to get to the story off the first couple of pages of Google result. But it didn't last long. Like, a couple of weeks later, they started
cues.zh: 你知道，他们创建博客，发布一些关于她喜欢猫、喜欢度假的美好而无害的故事之类的内容。他们成功把那则故事挤出了 Google 搜索结果的前几页。但这没持续多久。大概几周后，它就开始

cues.en: creeping back up to the top result.
cues.zh: 慢慢爬回搜索结果的最前面。

cues.en: Is this a totally lost battle?
cues.zh: 这是一场彻底没有胜算的战斗吗？

cues.en: You know, I think the very best thing we can do if you see a kind of, you know, an unfair or an ambiguous
cues.zh: 你知道，我觉得如果你看到某种不公平或模棱两可的

cues.en: shaming
cues.zh: 网络羞辱，

cues.en: is to speak up. Because I think the worst thing that happened to Justine was that nobody supported her, like, everyone was against her. That is profoundly
cues.zh: 最好的做法就是站出来发声。因为我觉得，发生在贾斯汀身上最糟糕的事，就是没有人支持她，所有人都在反对她。这会造成极大的

cues.en: traumatizing,
cues.zh: 心理创伤，

cues.en: you know, to be told by tens of thousands of people that you need to get out.
cues.zh: 你知道，被成千上万的人告诉你该滚出去，

cues.en: But if a shaming happens, then there's like a babble of voices, like in a democracy,
cues.zh: 但如果发生网络羞辱时，能有各种声音交织在一起，就像在民主社会里一样，

cues.en: where people are discussing it, I think that's much less damaging. So, you know, I think that's the way forward. But it's hard, because if you do stand up for somebody,
cues.zh: 大家一起讨论，我觉得造成的伤害就会小得多。所以，我觉得这才是未来该走的路。但这很难，因为如果你站出来支持某个人，

cues.en: you know, it's incredibly unpleasant. Okay. So let's talk about your experience, because you stood up while writing this book. By the way, it's mandatory reading for everybody. Okay? You stood up because the book actually puts the spotlight on shamers, And
cues.zh: 你知道，那会让人极其难受。好了，我们来谈谈你的经历，因为你在写这本书时站了出来。顺便说一句，这是所有人的必读书。好吗？你站出来，是因为这本书实际上把聚光灯打在了羞辱他人的人身上。而且

cues.en: I assume you didn't only have friendly reactions on Twitter. It didn't go down that well with
cues.zh: 我猜你在 Twitter 上得到的反应不全是友善的。这事并没有得到

cues.en: some people. I mean, lots of... You don't want to sort of just concentrate, because, you know, lots of people, you know, understood and were really nice about the book and so on. But yeah, for thirty years, I've been writing stories about abuses of power. And when I say, you know, the powerful people over there in the military or in the pharmaceutical industry, everybody applauds me. As soon as I say,
cues.zh: 一些人的认可。我的意思是，很多……你不会想只关注这一点，因为你知道，很多人理解这本书，也对它非常友善之类的。但没错，三十年来，我一直在写滥用权力的故事。当我说，你知道，那些在军队或制药行业中的有权势之人滥用权力时，所有人都会为我鼓掌。可一旦我说，

cues.en: we are the powerful people abusing our power now, I get people saying, well, you must be a racist too.
cues.zh: 现在是我们这些有权势的人在滥用权力，就有人对我说：那你肯定也是种族主义者。

cues.en: So the other night, were at... Yesterday, we were at dinner, and there were kind of two discussions going on. On one side, you were talking with people around the table, on the other, and that was a nice constructive discussion, on the other, every time you turn to your phone, there is this deluge of insults. Yeah. Yeah. This happened last night. We had, like, a TED dinner last night. So I was I was... We were chatting, it was lovely and nice, and then I decided to check Twitter. So I checked Twitter, and somebody said, were a white supremacist.
cues.zh: 前几天晚上，我们在……昨天，我们在吃晚饭，席间大概有两种对话。一边，你在和桌旁的人聊天，那是很好的建设性讨论；另一边，每次你转向手机，就会涌来一大堆辱骂。是的。是的。这发生在昨晚。昨晚我们有个类似 TED 晚宴。我当时……我们聊得很开心，然后我决定看看 Twitter。于是我看了 Twitter，有人说我是白人至上主义者。

cues.en: And then I went back and had a nice conversation with somebody, and then I went back to Twitter. Somebody said my very existence,
cues.zh: 然后我回去和某人聊得很愉快，然后又回到 Twitter。有人说我的存在本身，

cues.en: you know, made the world a worse place. You know, my friend Adam Curtis says that we're...
cues.zh: 你知道，让世界变得更糟。你知道，我朋友 Adam Curtis 说，我们……

cues.en: That maybe the Internet is like a John Carpenter movie from the nineteen eighties, when eventually, you know, everybody will start... Everyone's screaming at each other and shooting at each other, and eventually,
cues.zh: 也许互联网就像 80 年代 John Carpenter 的电影，最终，你知道，所有人都会开始……所有人互相尖叫、互相开枪，最终，

cues.en: everybody would flee to somewhere safer. And I'm starting to think of that as a really nice option.
cues.zh: 所有人都会逃到更安全的地方。我开始觉得这真是个不错的选择。

cues.en: John, thank you. Thank you, Bruno.
cues.zh: John，谢谢你。谢谢你，Bruno。
